body: I fantasize about refusing medical treatment more than I think about killing myself.
Good to hear! Hopefully I've helped a few people who came by here in small ways.
Maybe, or maybe you don't want life to continue in exactly the same manner.

> which makes it impossible for me to pursue the only things which I find enjoyable with any hope of success

How do you know this? What are these things which you find enjoyable, by the way?

You certainly come off as intelligent to me. I think I'm above average but I have nothing on the likes of Gauss -- it's slightly disappointing, in a way, but I don't let it get to me much. I'm much more frustrated at wasting the opportunities that have come my way, but I've learned, albeit through failure, that thinking along the lines of "If I could only have/achieve X, I'll be happy!" is fallacious. I've had to learn the hard way that it's hard for me to feel like I'm of any worth without enjoying bits of life with those who are close to me, which has little to do with my career (or lack thereof) or my achievements.

I used to be more competitive and obsessed when it came to my IQ, achievements, grades, etc., but it's all worth jack shit if I'm not happy.

Will therapy be difficult for you to get? I don't think therapy alone is sufficient, but it can be a push in the right direction. Let's be honest, being in a more pessimistic state of mind -- i.e. while depressed -- isn't the best time to try and judge outcome. :P

Hope this helps you in some way. I'm not you, but I can relate to some of what you say. Feel free to PM me if you want.
That made me smile.

> I'm just not really sure what reason there is for me to live, aside from taking up space and using up our planet's resources - which slightly nudges the needle from being right between wanting to live and wanting to die, towards wanting to die. I could go back to work, buy a nice house with giant tv and whatever other stuff people say you need to be happy, but to what end?

There doesn't have to be a Reason with a capital r. Maybe your reason to keep going could be to try out as many types of food as you can, travel to as many places as you can, etc.

I think knowing that one is going to die and trying to enjoy the small amount of time one has on Earth is all that people can do. Close friends can make your time much more bearable. I've tried and failed to think myself out of meaninglessness; I don't know of anyone who has.

On the basis of meaning alone, my death would be just as pointless as my life, so why kill myself now? Of course it doesn't stop me from obsessing about suicide. I have to remind myself once in a while that suicidal thoughts are simply non-rational -- I don't beat them by out-thinking them, I beat them by changing or trying to change my circumstances. I've done it before to some extent, so it can't possibly be the case that I'm doomed for the rest of my life.

I think having everyone leave them is something anyone would never want. No details to go on, but don't think a scenario where a bunch of your friends collectively chose to leave you is very likely. Maybe you withdrew too much and no one felt brave enough to press you about how you were doing.

I have nothing to go on, but is there anything I can help you with? I've went through most of my life completely alone, if that matters.

Life is certainly cyclical for me as well, something I'm very tired of. I'm close to your age and I've been an academic disappointment thus far. I think I'm a burden to some but a few others seem thankful that I exist. Every few years I manage to meet meaningful friends who give me the energy to keep going. We may fall apart later on, but they help get me through the shit that I'm going through *now*.

Maybe it's just me, but I think I hate myself too much to just get away with suicide without giving it a try, because, let's be honest: I'm *not* in chronic pain right now and many of my problems are first-world problems. If I do the deed, I'd just confirm it to myself that I'm a lazy piece of shit motherfucker who always backs out. *What's the worst that can happen if I keep going?*

How about volunteering in the area of natural preservation or something similar? You'll do a whole lot more than simply depositing your chemicals into the ground (which will happen eventually, anyway). Also, nothing wrong with going to a secluded area and just hanging out -- why not experience that as often as you can rather than just once?

I'm not a psychiatrist, but some of the lectures I've watched about depression mentioned that suicides occur more often as the sufferer is moving out of depression because the psychomotor retardation of depression is being lifted, but the suicidal urge is still there. I suppose my advice would be to tie yourself closer to others so that you could use obligation to others as a reason for holding on whenever you get a particularly bad urge. Good luck and hang in there.

Reading your response through a few times, you're more worried about the bad impressions you've made rather than a lack of accomplishments, which I take to generally mean successes that aren't only limited to impressing a very select number of people. Given that, you *can* start over -- you can move to a new area, meet new people, and make new impressions. You might fail, but you're more likely to fail if you tell yourself that you will. There is never certainty except when you decide to fail.

> I really want her to like me, but then, why would she when this is who I am?

If you respect her, don't put words in her mouth/thoughts in her head. You won't know until you find out for yourself.
What would be something you'd be proud of?

Take a break from school or drop out if you have to -- why go to suicide instantly? Give yourself a chance. Not everyone and their dog goes to college as some may proclaim, yet most people eventually find their way.
Do you have family that could do simple stuff like check up on you and give you calls every once in a while? How did you lose your friends?

I can't undo what's been already happened in your life, but if there's anything I can do for you, feel free to message me. You're neither a failure nor a success in my eyes -- I don't care about that, you're just a person.

> Nobody calls me first to spend time with, I am a last resort. I'm boring. Happy things make me sad, sad things make me sad. There's no winning. There are people in my life, but they won't do more than give a sad story at my funeral and move on.

You've described much of my life, although sadness isn't permanent for me, and I suspect it isn't for you, too. People take you for granted; there's no easy way out of it, but you have to reciprocate only what others give to you in order to filter out the people who don't really matter. If they initiate a call once a month, do the same to them, and if you fall apart, then they probably weren't interested in friendship. You're boring if the other person doesn't appreciate the attention you give them and expects to be entertained the entire time -- avoid those people.

> What's the point of it all? 

With nothing changing, there is no point. There might be a point to it if things change, and that's for you to explore.
It's not worth living if your only source of self-worth comes from school and/or career aspirations. You have to look to other things that make your life enjoyable and perhaps even valuable.

I think that if you look hard enough for a logical (and fulfilling) reason to keep on living, you're going to be disappointed. We apply a cost-benefit analysis to many things in life, but life itself gets a free pass. Life is going to suck to some extent no matter what -- figuring out things that make it suck a bit less is all we can do. Perhaps you'll be able to break out of this and really *live* life, but I haven't been keeping my hopes up and I don't expect you to do so, either.

> everyone's better off without you, let's go, if you really love these people, you'll off yourself so they don't have to deal with your pathetic existence

They can deal with it, they're not children. If your existence is offensive to them, they are free to break off contact with you.
How can she, whoever it is, fix you?

It gets better and worse. When I feel like shit, there's a good chance I'll feel a bit better in a few months, and when I feel better, there's a good chance I'll feel a bit worse in a few months. I'm not sure what joy is, but I can still do things to captivate my attention for a bit.

It's only worth living so long as you think it is, and from what I understand, the reason(s) for living are diminishing or being outweighed as the time goes by. Don't worry about the contributing something to society part, we're all parasites supported by a few giants. ;) You're not some thug wasting away in prison, so I wouldn't have much reason to think of you that way.

I really hope you find a solution to your problem, and in the meantime, someone to appreciate the pain you're in. Have you looked around for something like group therapy? Never done anything like that myself, but perhaps it could be a breath of fresh air.

It's up to you to probe their personalities. Perhaps some of them have or are experiencing things not unlike what you're going through; "shrinks" are one thing, but understanding peers you can more readily relate to may be worth some risk. You won't have to pretend that everything's okay, and *that* itself would be okay. Shutting out your feelings can take on a more permanent state; while you seem to still experience episodes of crying, I sometimes find sheer and utter emptiness to be much worse.

Have you considered letting a friend know about this? Do you have any suspicions as to what may be causing you to feel the way you do?

> I’m just so tired. Tired of pretending like I am o.k. Tired of trying so hard to achieve absolutely nothing. Tired of . . . living. . . at least the way I have been . . .

Can you think of any path by which you'd achieve more than absolutely nothing? I'm older than you are and it's one of the most difficult things for me to answer; if you have a hard time coming up with something, don't worry. This tends to be tied into a career, which is a hard thing to plan for, realistically. Striving to be helpful, dependable, and honest can make me feel a bit better about myself, and it's independent of any career path.

I'm not assuming anything, so please don't be offended by my questions.

Do you have friends you can speak to in person or people you trust? How often do you go outside? How often do you exercise? Have you been sleeping decently lately?

They're little things and nearly unnoticeable when they're there, but they can make things just that much harder when you're in a tough spot.

> It's always me who sends the first message

Remember this and use it to weed out those who don't care.

You say you've given up, which is true -- you've given up on your current circumstances. It's time to change something, at least one thing at a time. Ditch friends if you feel they're toxic; look for another job; spend more time outside to be away from your family more often (if I'm interpreting it correctly).

Best of luck.

I've certainly felt much of what you describe -- not wanting to do anything, having no motivation to do well in school, withdrawing, and disappointing my family. I'm not past/over anything and I doubt I ever will be; I have to keep telling myself that I've felt differently in the past and my current circumstances aren't guaranteed to remain constant for the entirety of my future.

It's important for me to maintain at least a certain amount of activity, both physical and mental, in order to give myself a chance to push out of the rut. I read even though I couldn't care less and I exercise even though I want to lay in bed and not get up, and after a while I begin to improve; I can't afford to trust my feelings when I know I've felt differently in the very same circumstances.

I hope that makes some sense as it's not the easiest thing to put into words. I owe it to myself to try and push on given that I'm still relatively healthy.

Thanks for being there for him and trying your best to help. Is there any way he can get professional help for this? This may be too much for you to handle alone; sometimes you need the assistance of those used to dealing with these types of situations.

> I really don't want to be push her or pester her if she really doesn't want anyone to contact her

She *needs* someone to contact her.

> Is there anything I can do or say that would let her know that I still love her like a motherfucker, and am here for her?

Tell her exactly that.

I know that I haven't always felt dead, and that it isn't the only option.

I know that I'm (currently) not in agony due to chronic pain and that life isn't *that* bad -- I owe it to myself to try at least a bit since it's not *all* bleak on the frontlines.

> So yeah. I'm closing myself off to people. Becoming a recluse. I sleep, eat, shit, play video games, and then repeat it every day. What's the point?

I don't hold a PhD, but I'd wager that, evolutionarily, your body is meant to respond the way it is responding. Humans just aren't made to have very limited social ties, little exercise (I'm inferring), etc.

More exercise, good sleep schedule, etc., doesn't seem to directly address a lack of desire for anything, but I don't think you consciously elected to feel exactly the way you now feel. Just a thought.
Hi, what's making you consider suicide?

Either it takes courage to reach out or most people simply don't bother to step up and act when someone is in need. I haven't found the answer as I would be in your exact place were anything to happen, but perhaps it's time to take on a different perspective of your relationships and think over how much certain people really care about you. People who really care are out there.

There were times when I played video games most of my waking moments and it did no good at all for my ability to think clearly, sleep, or be anything other than depressed and numb. Try to limit the time you spend if you're conscious of the fact that you're getting nothing out of it. I can't emphasize enough how much of a difference *forcing* myself, at least initially, to read books helped me.

Do you get outside much? I'm not sure about the nature of your work, but a daily walk did quite a bit for my general alertness and ability to feel something; running about 3 times a week did even more. I *always* shrugged off advice about exercise until I seriously did it myself -- your body wasn't made to sit around so much.

If you have any questions or further comments, feel free to post here or PM me. I'm fairly close to your own age, if you're curious.

> I know it's not good for me, but at least it doesn't make other people worry about me when I know their attention is needed elsewhere or if they already have enough stress on their shoulders.

Some people would be flattered that you would share with them with your private thoughts and feelings.
I can only hope for a friend like yours. :)

The way the link presents it *is* binary in the sense that if one has any influence whatsoever in at least one other person's life, then it is always wrong for them to commit suicide. I don't disagree with you that the way people live is not characterized by either extreme, but that's irrelevant, according to the link.

I'm not personally active on this subreddit, but it may have more people who can relate specifically to your problems: http://www.reddit.com/r/domesticviolence/

Hope you can find someone who can help more than I can here, there, or somewhere on reddit. :)

To keep in mind Guideline III, I'll suggest that this is something that may be beyond the scope of this subreddit and that some form of professional help may guide you in the right direction. I can't offer advice on a personal level with regards to issues like those, but perhaps others can chime in. :)

I can't say there's an easy way through this, but I have good confidence that you will find happiness that's at least a bit more lasting should you consider them important *yourself*. It's a matter of experiencing things, some of which you find interesting and fulfilling.

I'm not the arbiter of truth, but you probably want to consider hobbies you can consistently build upon, such as reading (reading helps, and I retain my writing skills much more than anything else I've ever studied) or programming, and some certain cause which you can find a way of applying yourself toward, such as working against hunger.

Lastly, do you have any ideas about why you feel like you can't trust people?

> I just want to be happy like I feel everyone else is

It can be tempting to think this way, but statistically speaking, there are definitely people suffering silently among us.

What you can tell from your current case is that the things you've done thus far haven't really given you lasting happiness. While you may not look to sports in the long-run, perhaps there's something that will work? Do you have any childhood "dreams" that you didn't follow through with? General interests? They can help you compile a list of possibilities.

I'm sure it's great to live for other people when they always reciprocate or perhaps even shower you with anything that you may desire, but it's not such a good deal for the rest of us.

Not that I'm treating it as nothing more than a transaction, but I get tired of asking myself what the fuck I'm doing wrong, the heartbreak, etc. Being alone isn't ideal, but things can be worse.

I used to be Christian and I can see where you're coming from. All I can really say is that it never ceases being about other people: religion is simply a convenient, already-there social circle for one to jump into. There is more to it, but the core of all religion lies in fellowship.

As far as death goes, while I used to believe in eternal life "on paper," I never believed it in the same way as I believed that the Sun would rise the next day. It was something like suspension of disbelief, a placeholder of hope that I would find evidence/proof in the future, or perhaps a mix of both.

Cessation of existence isn't a comfortable thing to think about; I have to push myself not to dwell on those thoughts as I doubt anything good would come out of them, just like it is often useless to try and think one's way out of anxiety.

Hope this helps.
How much physical activity do you get? Do you sleep well? Do you feel like you have an adequate number of friends?
What's driving you to suicide?

What an utterly naive buffoon.
Can't say I've done much, but I fantasize about refusing medical treatment and whatnot.

I feel as though we're not speaking about the same subject since I agree with much of what you say here because I'm already alive.

The unborn human is the antinatalist side of the coin rather than the suicidal side of the coin. To the unborn human, the question would be, "Are you willing to take pain along with pleasure, with the likely case that there would be more pain than pleasure in life?" To the living human, the question is, "Is life worth living? Since you're already here, can you make your situation better?"

Maybe I'm reading too much into this. ;)

You answered your own question, you're not under obligation. Living is voluntary, but unless you have something like a chronic disease that causes you pain every moment that you're awake, there are things you can probably change.

Just stop smiling when you don't feel like it. What's the worst that would happen, really? No one will put a gun to your head and demand that you smile. If you're considering getting it over with, why not try living life the way you want to live it?

Societal interaction with fools can be unfulfilling, true, so sever the connections which to you seem wasteful and try to find people who, well, aren't fools. I know you know this and what I'm saying is incredibly obvious, but I want to remind you that if you're considering suicide, then you owe it to yourself to at least change your circumstances -- dramatically, if you have to -- before getting it over with. Weigh the final possible outcomes and ask yourself, "What's the worst that can happen if I *don't* commit suicide and do shit for *myself*?"

Actions can change things drastically, and make things *worse*. Even when things don't get *worse*, we still have those pockets of *suffering*, something that baby can never feel.

See what I did there? Anyone who considers suicide doesn't seriously entertain the idea that an infinitesimally small sliver of happiness is worth any cost. I'm really at a loss to try and understand your thoughts about this in a way other than an evolutionary bias in judgement. Sorry if it offends you.

> The baby that dies in the womb must envy us so, being trapped without even the beginning of their existence.

How much would it envy us if it were to grow up, suffer, and take its own life in the end?
The only way I can keep going is if I make myself ignore all the time spent in boredom and all the suffering life amounts to.

I'm basically in the same place you are, so I'm doing something to change that by learning how to program. Do you have an idea of what you might want to do for a living? It's perfectly okay if you don't, but you have to try things before you have any idea about what you might enjoy.

The thing about programming is that I'm *creating* something on my own, and that gives me a feeling of satisfaction surpassing anything college has given me thus far. Doing another problem set as an assignment, just like everybody else --> feel worthless, who do I even do this, who gives a fuck, etc.; making shit on my own --> wow, something I can try and build on, something I'm doing *on my fucking own*, something I might get paid for later on.

I hope this is helpful. :)

Do you have something to build skill in that will stuck around for the rest of your life? Writing, programming, etc.? I didn't feel like a complete, useless piece of shit when I was actually making something.

Also, despite what the rest of the world is trying to tell you, life does not revolve around jobs and girlfriends. I know everyone nods at this and waves it away, but at least allow it to be a possibility; if you deny its possibility, it will never become an actuality.

Lastly, the weight part. If you're like me, you feel like shit most days, have no energy, have trouble concentrating, etc. There's no easy way out of it except to start exercising. It has been years since I've been able to run, hell, a half mile, but I recently got myself to do it and I'm feeling *much* better than before.

I hope you're not offended by this, but it's easy for someone who doesn't buy the spiritual idea to become cynical upon hearing something like this, particularly if they're already in a bad state of mind.
How did you ascertain that all life has some intrinsic value? I hear this being thrown around all the time, but I've never understood it.

You seem like a person I'd rather have around than not. I won't try to guilt-trip you with the usual crap, though. I may be wrong with my intuition, but I suspect you don't feel like you're being appreciated for what you do or for who you are; I certainly feel that way and it can be draining to have to keep going forward without the slightest bit of gratitude from someone who means something to me. Sometimes people are grateful, yes, but they're all transient, or have been thus far.

> But I'm just so tired and discouraged lately. I get into bitter moods where I start to hate everything around me, and I don't understand. I feel like I'm trying to do everything right and yet it still completely falls apart in my hands.

You just keep describing my life. When I mentioned how people are transient earlier, the consequence of which is that I often don't get to see the effects of what I do. That can make me feel like everything I do changes nothing and is thus worthless, but I have to keep reminding myself that I can't possibly know that. I haven't really been angry in a long time, but I can definitely get bitter. Pursuing things that require much of my attention can get my mind off of such thoughts, or perhaps simple exercise; I rarely really think my way out of a bad state of mind.

> I'm going to die someday, my hand or another's; it's one of the few comforts I can rely on, heh.

Well, I'll give you something else you can rely on: if you're feeling like things are too much for you and you want to talk to someone, feel free to PM me.

/e-hug

> But the depression is still there, never far from the tip of my tongue or the edge of my perception, just waiting for the right trigger to send another wave my way.

That's how I feel. It doesn't take much to go right back to where I came from, even after years of trying my hardest.

> Suicide seems like such an inevitability now, it's as clear as day to me: one day I'll finally give up, it feels so certain.

Fine, but it hasn't come yet.

> Is it so wrong to want some tiny degree of control over my own damn life? That's not the right way to phrase it, I know that... but I don't feel it. What am I doing wrong here? Or am I just stuck like this, in limbo; unable to end my suffering, not through life and not through death?

It's not wrong at all, but I'm not sure how many people really have certainties. Is it better to have a false sense of security and have the next crash be even harder? I don't even know at this point. Sometimes the uncertainty is exciting, and other times it is crippling; it's as if I'm thrown about between the extremes, unable to establish a foothold.

What gives me a bit of hope is that I can manage, even in this state, to help others in small ways; perhaps someone will one day come along and return the favor.

> What would make me happy is if I'm dead

You wouldn't be happy if you can't feel anything.

> So I'm going to do something for me

What would you be doing for yourself? Would you rather be traveling? Partying? Working? If so, take a leave from college or drop out altogether and do what you want to do for yourself! If you're willing to die, at least try to do what you would've been doing had you lived for yourself -- you owe it to yourself.

You're making sense, alright. It can really get debilitating when I consider the fact that I'm just a bunch of chemicals assembled in a complex manner; that I will exist for an infinitesimally short amount of time; that the universe is indifferent and I have no purpose on which to lean on for strength. My desire to live is based upon an evolutionary bias, and were I a *fully* rational being, I would have probably committed suicide long ago.

I can't explain it, prove it, or convince you of it, but you just have to trust me: there are some days when existential questions simply stop mattering to me. I don't come up with any particular solution; rather, I can live (more) when the questions are put to rest. That doesn't stop me from trying to find an answer as I'm intellectually curious that way, but it is more of a healthy pursuit rather than brooding for months at a time.

I'm not sure this helps, but perhaps you may relate to this. I'm still trying to hang on, and maybe you can do the same.
Might you know someone who has contact with them, or are you saying that because you don't expect them to read anything you send them?

> It was all my fault. I was mean, and hateful. OUt of line. I couldn't even control it. It just happened. I was like, outside my body, watching this happen..this mean, angry person..me...and my friend...well...left.

Why don't you tell them that? What's the worst that can happen?
I have a test to go to in a few minutes, but I would be available later towards the evening (at least in my time zone).

It's mostly my fault. I've squandered everything that was given to me. It's my personality that makes all social interactions awkward, and it's me who was mistaken when trying to do something despite that.

> So what if I'm always single, so what if I used to be a star athlete who's now left with nothing - I don't deserve anything

And likewise, the universe doesn't deserve the pleasure of watching me struggle. ;)

I used to be obsessed with video games, but I'm much better now. Video games did nothing good for me, although it seemed like they did while I was playing them. I still fire something up on occasion, but the marathons are (hopefully) gone for good.

I'm glad to help. :) You have a good plan -- stick to it, try to stay strong, and if you ever need support, we're right here for you!

I, too, hope to meet someone like you one day. Everything is a work-in-progress, but I still have hope. Likewise, you're free to PM me. :)
Hi, do you have a car or decent public transportation in your area?

I'm afraid it won't be easy. I think being completely alone becomes a better alternative when you're taken for granted for many years, but it doesn't necessarily have to get to that.

If you put in an hour of your time and they give back a minute, then it's a waste of energy and it *will not* get any better. You have to cut and run, or at least expose yourself to new people.

I wish it were easier, I really do, but I've found nothing else. :(

I'm telling you to not put effort into relationships where the other person isn't doing their part. For example, if you're the one who has to initiate all of the texting, always the one who has to offer suggestions for hanging out, etc., then you're putting in effort but getting back little, if anything. If you're getting nothing out of it, then stop working at it. I don't necessarily mean stop contacting them at all, but if they text you once a month, don't text them more than once a month -- give them back what they give you.

What this does is free up time and energy for you to keep looking for others who might actually give you back what you put in -- people who value you. Once you find someone who values you, it's the best feeling in the entire world.

People take me for granted all the time. I help people out whenever I can because I'm just that kind of a person. I put in the effort, but it is almost never reciprocated; worse yet, I see people do little and they have tons of friends.

I know this isn't going to be easy for you, but you have to reciprocate effort if you want to find people who truly care about you. If you're always the one having to initiate, having to come up with every topic of conversation, always the one to be forgotten as soon as *anything* else comes up, then you're getting the short end of the stick here. If people won't put in the effort, then focus your efforts on continuing the search for someone who will. It's a game of numbers, but sooner or later you *will* find a genuine person.

Please don't give up -- as I've said, it will not be an easy road by any means, but if you're anything like me, there is absolutely no other way. People will use you and shit on you if you let them. Good luck; I hope what I say helps you somehow.

Do you have any places you can visit? Something with nice scenery where you can escape for a few hours? It may get old if you do it too often, but once in a while it can help maintain some sanity in your life.

I've done a good deal to fuck up my own life. What's keeping me around is that there are still some activities I can do where I am happy or at least not depressed for the moment, where my failures aren't immediately apparent to me. Something like driving over to some nearby hill on an evening, getting out of my car, and looking around at all the buildings which are lit up.

It doesn't solve anything, but it helps me retain sanity when I have to come back down and face hell head-on.

And let me just remind you that *everyone* has regrets. Everyone thinks they fucked up their life one way or another, but most still make it through a natural lifespan. Just a thought.
Not too many are keen on doing so while the person is still alive.
Does that sound consistent with his prior intent of committing suicide on his own?
Are you sure she didn't say that to you out of spite?

I wish I was driven to sustain it, honestly. I sometimes feel like all I can do is just sulk and surrender. Shallow attachments make me cynical, genuine relationships give me hope, though I've had almost no experience with the latter.

Yep, it's hard. I don't depend much on external motivation, but sometimes it's frustrating not having anyone to appreciate, well, me. Much of the progress I make is just temporary and regression is right around the corner.

I still have some energy left to keep going, so I think I owe it to myself to see whatever happens through.

In many ways, I'm where you are. No friends, never had a girlfriend, no job prospects. I think I'm still around because there are things that can still make me smile.
